personas.role: Approves mandates on a Trusted Surface: exact purchases when present, limits for the agent when not.
goals: Let an agent buy within limits I set
Have evidence if a purchase goes wrong
pains: No way to cancel an open mandate before it expires
Limits written in constraint terms are hard to read
Unclear who pays if the agent misreads me
implements: Nothing technical: approves on a wallet, issuer app, browser or agent app that acts as Trusted Surface
mustTrust: The Trusted Surface to show the real checkout
The agent to stay inside its constraints
questions: What exactly did I approve, and for how long?
Can the agent spend twice from one approval?
What happens when the agent finds something outside my limits?

Prefer short expiry times for autonomous tasks
Keep the receipts the agent stores
metrics: Time from task to approved purchase
Number of fallbacks to manual approval
personas.story: Priya asks her assistant to buy a two-person tent before Friday, under 300 dollars, from one of two outdoor stores. Her banking app opens and shows the limits in plain words, the stores, the price ceiling and an expiry on Friday night. She confirms with her fingerprint and goes to work. On Wednesday the agent finds the green tent for 249 dollars and buys it without asking. On Thursday it tries a matching groundsheet, but the store answers that the item is outside the approved line items, so her phone asks her to approve that one directly. She declines. Both receipts sit in the app.

No revocation primitive for open mandates
Specification moved to FIDO with no public draft
implements: Payment Receipt handling and error codes
OpenID4VP delegation with type delegate when acting as wallet
mustTrust: The user credential issuer or the trusted agent provider list
The network to honor scoped credentials
Its own deterministic code, never an LLM
questions: How do I track payment.budget across presentations?
Which delegation model do my verifiers accept?
How do I invalidate tokens from overlapping mandates?
firstSteps: Read agent_authorization.md and payment_mandate.md at v0.2.0
Run the Python SDK chain verification against the schema examples
Map each failure to invalid_credential, invalid_mandate or unresolved_constraint

Token issuance latency after mandate verification
personas.story: Marco runs the agent payments team at a digital wallet. Each morning he reviews rejected presentations by error code. Most invalid_credential cases come from one agent provider whose closed mandates are signed with a rotated key that no longer matches cnf. The unresolved_constraint cases are mostly budget checks: his service is the one that has to remember earlier presentations, and the specification never said whose job that was. He files a note for the FIDO payments group about revocation, then adds a rule that invalidates outstanding tokens when the agent presents an overlapping mandate. The release goes out with ES256 keys only.

pains: Liability stays with network rules that are not yet agent specific

How do I challenge the user if v0.2 has no step-up?

personas.story: Helen handles disputes at a regional bank. A customer says her agent bought the wrong concert tickets. The merchant supplies the Checkout Mandate and receipt, and the network passes the Payment Mandate. Helen's tool recomputes the hash of the checkout JWT, matches both receipt references and confirms that the agent's closed mandate sits inside the customer's open one, with the venue and price allowed. The evidence shows the agent stayed inside its limits, so the dispute turns on whether those limits matched what the customer meant. AP2 cannot answer that, and the network rules say nothing specific about agents yet. She escalates it.

personas.story: Tomas leads checkout engineering at an outdoor retailer that sells through UCP. His team signs every checkout with ES256 because the specification forbids deterministic signatures, even though their bot-auth setup already uses Ed25519, so they now manage two key types. Today an agent presents a closed Checkout Mandate for a tent, but the cart has a different color than the open mandate allows. His service evaluates checkout.line_items, finds no match and returns a Checkout Receipt with unresolved_constraint. Ten minutes later the same order comes back with a user-signed closed mandate and goes through. He logs the round trip for the weekly report.

Put signing behind a deterministic service with no LLM access
personas.story: Aiko builds a grocery agent. Her signer is a small service the model cannot call directly: the model proposes a basket, deterministic code checks it against the open mandates and only then signs a closed mandate with the key in cnf. Today a store returned unresolved_constraint because a substitute brand was not in acceptable_items. Her code stored the error receipt, asked the user's phone for approval of the exact basket, and finished. She is also adding scope reduction: after each success the agent records the open, closed and receipt tuple, so the weekly budget is never presented twice.

Who keeps mandates and for how long?
firstSteps: Read Dispute Evidence and Security and Privacy Considerations
Map open mandates to your SCA and authorization rules
Set a retention rule for mandates and receipts
personas.story: Sophie reviews a plan to accept agent purchases at a European retailer. The mandates help: a signed record of what the customer saw and approved, with only the needed fields disclosed. But AP2 itself claims no compliance. Its glossary defines Strong Customer Authentication and dynamic linking without saying a mandate satisfies them, and whether a standing open mandate counts as consent to a specific transaction under PSD2 is untested. She asks the team to keep mandates and receipts for the dispute window, to treat risk_data as personal data, and to follow the FIDO working group because the specification no longer evolves on GitHub.
